content: Eposino is a recombinant human erythropoietin (EPO) injection designed for administration either intravenously (IV) or subcutaneously (SC). It is manufactured by Shandong Kexing Bioproducts Co., Ltd., a biotechnology company formed as a joint venture between Peking University Weiming Group and Sinogen (China) Ltd. Erythropoietin, the active ingredient in Eposino, is produced using recombinant DNA technology in mammalian cell cultures. Clinically, it is utilized to treat anemia caused by chronic kidney disease or cancer chemotherapy. Additionally, EPO is widely recognized as a performance-enhancing drug in endurance sports. Eposino is available in vials or pre-filled single-use syringes. The Eposino rediject syringe is specifically designed to minimize drug wastage by eliminating dead space in the syringe chamber, which can otherwise result in the loss of up to 10% of the total dosage. Moreover, the syringe is equipped with a double-beveled thin needle, which reduces pain during injection and lowers the risk of iatrogenic infections. Eposino.com, the exclusive online distributor of Eposino, became the first platform to offer recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) for global purchase via the internet in the mid-2000s. The website claims to provide customers with a secure, private, and reliable method to purchase rhEPO remotely, with expedited delivery to their chosen destination through express courier services. Eposino is a registered and licensed pharmaceutical product in numerous countries, including India. In India, it is distributed to pharmacies and healthcare institutions by Hindustan Bio Sciences, a Hyderabad-based company with a share capital of $2.5 million USD. Despite its clinical applications, the Eposino brand has been associated with controversy. Reports have indicated that the notorious Spanish doping doctor, Eufemiano Fuentes, preferred the Chinese-manufactured Eposino for use with his clients, who included prominent professional cyclists such as Ivan Basso, Jan Ullrich, and Jörg Jaksche. Additionally, Eposino.com published an unauthorized English translation of the book L.A. Confidential: Lance Armstrong's Secrets (L.A. Confidentiel: Les secrets de Lance Armstrong), which was made available for download as a four-part Adobe PDF file.
